description: Conditional expectation properties from Saporito Ch 2.1 (measure_theory).

theorems.name: Linearity of Conditional Expectation
theorems.description: Proposition 2.1.5(2): E[αX + Y | G] = αE[X|G] + E[Y|G] a.s.

code.lean:
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic

open MeasureTheory

-- Linearity of conditional expectation: μ[c•f + g | m] =ᵐ[μ] c•μ[f|m] + μ[g|m]
-- Uses Mathlib's `condExp_add` and `condExp_smul`.
theorem condexp_linear {α : Type*} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
    (f g : α → ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (hf : Integrable f μ) (hg : Integrable g μ) :
    μ[c • f + g | m] =ᵐ[μ] c • μ[f | m] + μ[g | m] := by
  have h1 : μ[c • f + g | m] =ᵐ[μ] μ[c • f | m] + μ[g | m] :=
    condExp_add (hf.smul c) hg m
  have h2 : μ[c • f | m] =ᵐ[μ] c • μ[f | m] := condExp_smul c f m
  filter_upwards [h1, h2] with x hx1 hx2
  rw [hx1, Pi.add_apply, hx2]
  rfl

theorems.name: Tower Property
theorems.description: Proposition 2.1.11(6), the TOWER direction: for H ⊆ G ⊆ F, E[E[X|G] | H] = E[X|H] a.s. The companion equality E[E[X|H] | G] = E[X|H] (pulling out the coarser conditioning) is not delivered by this entry.

code.lean:
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic

open MeasureTheory

-- Tower property: μ[μ[f|m₂]|m₁] =ᵐ[μ] μ[f|m₁] for m₁ ≤ m₂.
-- (Mathlib statement is almost-everywhere equality.)
theorem condexp_tower {α : Type*} {m₁ m₂ m₀ : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
    (hm₁₂ : m₁ ≤ m₂) (hm₂ : m₂ ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm₂)]
    {f : α → ℝ} :
    μ[μ[f | m₂] | m₁] =ᵐ[μ] μ[f | m₁] :=
  condExp_condExp_of_le hm₁₂ hm₂

theorems.name: Pulling Out What's Known
theorems.description: Proposition 2.1.11(7): If Y is G-measurable and XY ∈ L¹, then E[XY | G] = Y · E[X | G]

code.lean:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory

-- Pulling out a known factor: μ[f * g | m] =ᵐ[μ] f * μ[g | m]
-- when f is m-strongly-measurable. Uses Mathlib's `condExp_mul_of_stronglyMeasurable_left`.
theorem condexp_pull_out {α : Type*} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α}
    {f g : α → ℝ}
    (hf : StronglyMeasurable[m] f) (hfg : Integrable (f * g) μ) (hg : Integrable g μ) :
    μ[f * g | m] =ᵐ[μ] f * μ[g | m] :=
  condExp_mul_of_stronglyMeasurable_left hf hfg hg

theorems.name: Independence Implies E[X|G] = E[X]
theorems.description: Proposition 2.1.11(8): If X is independent of G, then E[X | G] = E[X] a.s.

code.lean:
import Mathlib.Probability.ConditionalExpectation

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

-- Independence ⇒ μ[f | m₂] =ᵐ[μ] (fun _ => ∫ x, f x ∂μ).
-- Mathlib's `condExp_indep_eq` requires: f is m₁-measurable and m₁ ⊥ m₂.
theorem condexp_indep {Ω E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E]
    {m₁ m₂ m : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} {f : Ω → E}
    (hle₁ : m₁ ≤ m) (hle₂ : m₂ ≤ m) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hle₂)]
    (hf : StronglyMeasurable[m₁] f) (hindp : Indep m₁ m₂ μ) :
    μ[f | m₂] =ᵐ[μ] fun _ => μ[f] :=
  condExp_indep_eq hle₁ hle₂ hf hindp

theorems.name: Conditional Jensen's Inequality
theorems.description: Proposition 2.1.11(9): For convex φ: ℝ → ℝ, E[φ(X) | G] ≥ φ(E[X | G]) a.s.

code.lean:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory

/-- Proposition 2.1.11(9), conditional Jensen's inequality: for convex
    `φ : ℝ → ℝ` with `X` and `φ ∘ X` integrable,
    `φ(E[X | m]) ≤ᵐ E[φ(X) | m]`. Direct invocation of Mathlib's
    `ConvexOn.map_condExp_le_of_finiteDimensional` at `E = ℝ` — bare convexity
    suffices (convex functions on a finite-dimensional space are continuous,
    hence lower-semicontinuous); Mathlib does the real work. -/
theorem conditional_jensen_inequality
    {α : Type*} {m₀ : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : Measure α} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {m : MeasurableSpace α} (hm : m ≤ m₀) {φ : ℝ → ℝ} {X : α → ℝ}
    (hφ_cvx : ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ φ)
    (hX_int : Integrable X μ)
    (hφX_int : Integrable (φ ∘ X) μ) :
    φ ∘ μ[X | m] ≤ᵐ[μ] μ[φ ∘ X | m] := by
  haveI : SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm) := inferInstance
  exact hφ_cvx.map_condExp_le_of_finiteDimensional hm hX_int hφX_int

theorems.name: The Freezing Lemma (Independence Lemma, Unconditional Form)
theorems.description: For independent random variables X and Y on a finite measure space and g integrable against the product of their laws, E[g(X, Y)] = ∫ E[g(x, Y)] d(law X)(x): X can be frozen at a value x, g(x, Y) averaged over Y alone, and the result averaged over the law of X. This is the unconditional form; the conditional statement E[g(X, Y) | 𝒢] = G(X), for X 𝒢-measurable and Y independent of 𝒢, is ce-conditional-freezing-lemma.

metadata.reference: Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance II, Lemma 2.3.4 (independence lemma), unconditional form
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: independence makes the joint law the product of the marginal laws (Mathlib's IndepFun.map_prod_eq_prod_map_map), then the integral against the product measure is an iterated integral (integral_prod), and the inner integral is transported back along Y (integral_map). Holds for any value space of X; integrable_prod_map_of_countable checks the product integrability one value at a time when X is countable-valued. The conditional form is ce-conditional-freezing-lemma. Lives in MathFin/Foundations/IndepFreezing.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: The Independence Lemma (Conditional Freezing Lemma)
theorems.description: Let 𝒢 be a sub-σ-algebra, X a 𝒢-measurable random variable with values in a measurable space, and Y a random variable independent of 𝒢 (a.e.-measurable, with values in another measurable space), on a finite measure space. For g strongly measurable, with values in a Banach space, and g(X, Y) integrable, E[g(X, Y) | 𝒢] = G(X) almost surely, where G(x) = ∫ g(x, y) d(law Y)(y): given 𝒢, X is known and Y keeps its law. With vector-valued X and Y this is Shreve's independence lemma. It is the step that prices an option at an intermediate date: the state is known, and the increment to maturity is independent of the past (the American put's Brownian transitions, and the jump-diffusion prices of mf-jump-diffusion-payoff-every-date).

code.lean:
import MathFin.Foundations.IndepFreezing

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory

/-- **The independence lemma** (conditional freezing lemma): for `X` measurable for `m` and `Y`
independent of `m`, `𝔼[g(X, Y) | m] = G(X)` with `G(x) = ∫ g(x, y) d(law Y)(y)`. -/
theorem conditional_freezing_lemma_thm {Ω α β E : Type*} {m mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
    {mα : MeasurableSpace α} {mβ : MeasurableSpace β} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [CompleteSpace E] {P : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure P] (hm : m ≤ mΩ) {X : Ω → α} {Y : Ω → β}
    (hX : Measurable[m] X) (hY : AEMeasurable Y P)
    (hi : Indep (MeasurableSpace.comap Y mβ) m P) {g : α × β → E} (hg : StronglyMeasurable g)
    (hgi : Integrable (fun ω ↦ g (X ω, Y ω)) P) :
    P[fun ω ↦ g (X ω, Y ω) | m] =ᵐ[P] fun ω ↦ ∫ y, g (X ω, y) ∂(P.map Y) :=
  MathFin.condExp_comp_prodMk_of_indep hm hX hY hi hg hgi

metadata.reference: Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance II, Lemma 2.3.4 (independence lemma)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. On each event s ∈ 𝒢 the joint law of (X, Y) under P restricted to s is the law of X there times the law of Y: on rectangles, P(s ∩ X⁻¹A ∩ Y⁻¹B) = P(s ∩ X⁻¹A)·P(Y⁻¹B) because s ∩ X⁻¹A ∈ 𝒢 is independent of Y⁻¹B, and a measure on a product is determined by rectangles (Measure.prod_eq; map_restrict_prodMk_of_indep). So g is integrable against that product, and Fubini (integral_prod) with integral_map gives ∫_s g(X, Y) dP = ∫_s G(X) dP on every s ∈ 𝒢. G(X) is 𝒢-measurable (the section integral of a strongly measurable g is strongly measurable, StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right'), so it is the conditional expectation (ae_eq_condExp_of_forall_setIntegral_eq). Mathlib's condExp_prod_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib conditions on σ(X) through the conditional distribution; here the σ-algebra is any 𝒢 for which X is measurable and of which Y is independent, and the kernel is the law of Y. Lives in MathFin/Foundations/IndepFreezing.lean. Axioms-clean.
